title: Dispatch list from a re-sent feed
prompt: The order feed sends an order again every time its status or total changes, and the dispatch team only needs each order once. Write `solve(orders)` so it returns `order_id`, `customer_id`, `order_date` and `channel`, one row per order.
rules: Every copy of an order has the same `customer_id`, `order_date` and `channel`. Only `status` and `total` can change.
Return each `order_id` once, with the four columns in that order. Different orders stay separate, even when their other values match.
Missing values count as matching when comparing copies.
hints: Copies of a changed order differ in `status` or `total`, so they aren't exact copies of each other and `distinct()` on the whole table keeps them all.
`orders.dropDuplicates(["order_id"])` keeps one row per order, whichever copy Spark picks.
Which copy is kept doesn't matter here, because the columns you return are the same on every copy. Selecting those four columns and then calling `distinct()` works too.
starter:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F


def solve(orders):
    # Return each order once with order_id, customer_id, order_date and channel.
    return orders
explanation: The copies of a changed order aren't exact copies, so `distinct()` on the whole table keeps every version. Deduplicate on the key instead: `orders.dropDuplicates(["order_id"]).select("order_id", "customer_id", "order_date", "channel")`. Spark doesn't promise which copy it keeps, and that's fine here, because the four columns returned are the same on every copy. Returning `status` or `total` from that row would not be safe, since they depend on which copy survived. `orders.select("order_id", "customer_id", "order_date", "channel").distinct()` gives the same rows and never depends on the kept copy at all.
